info.title: ha-paneld
info.description: Local HTTP control API for the ha-paneld Home Assistant dashboard app. Plain HTTP on the LAN. Relaxed mode keeps the trusted-LAN workflow. Optional Hardened mode requires physical access for selected high-impact remote requests: someone must approve them on the panel's screen, and they cannot be approved remotely. The canonical machine API lives under /api/v1; the pre-0.8.5 flat paths respond 308 Permanent Redirect to their /api/v1 homes (method + body preserved). Exceptions: GET /health and POST /play are also served directly at the root for plain-curl automations and monitors.

DisplayGeometry.description: The panel's physical display and its logical rendering density, kept separate. Logical DPI is a rendering setting, never measured pixel density; physical_size is omitted whenever no trustworthy profile evidence selects this panel.

physical_pixels.description: The physical display mode, unaffected by any wm size or wm density override.

physical_size.description: Active display area from the profile variant matching this panel's product identity and physical pixels. A legacy profile physical_ppi value appears here with evidence approximate.

ppi.description: Physical pixel density derived from physical pixels and the active size.

evidence.description: measured: direct measurement; module: identified LCD module data; specification: manufacturer specification; approximate: not to be read as a measurement.

logical_dpi.description: Android rendering densities. None of these is physical pixel density.

factory_base.description: Android's factory reset logical DPI: the wm density reset reference (labelled Physical density) that display sizing restores, or the framework's stable density where the panel has no privilege to read it.

profile_factory_base.description: The factory-base logical DPI the matched profile variant declares.

current.description: The logical DPI rendering now, after any override.

recommended.description: The profile's dashboard-sizing preset; a preference, not a measurement.

viewport_dp.description: The rendered screen in density-independent pixels at the current logical DPI. Omitted when the current DPI is unreadable.

ProfileRef.description: Identifies one exact profile revision, as returned by every read route's `ref` field.

PanelAssistantDevice.description: A bounded, presentation-only projection of the panel's own device identity, for one Home Assistant device card. Reading it resolves nothing and writes nothing. Every property is optional: a value the panel cannot state safely is omitted rather than sent blank, so an empty object is valid. It carries no Android id, no MAC address and no serial number.

manufacturer.description: Hardware manufacturer: the configured override, else the active device profile's, else Android's own.

model.description: Product model with the ha-paneld application marker removed: the configured override, else the active device profile's, else Android's own model.

area.description: The panel's requested Home Assistant area; a suggestion, never authority.

HomeUiProof.description: Fresh post-install HOME and foreground observation, returned only for /api/v1/status?home_proof=1. Installers fail closed if it is missing, blocked or unknown.

PanelAssistantUpdate.description: A bounded projection of the panel's already-cached stable ha-paneld update observation. Reading it never resolves a release, changes channel, or starts an install. state=none means no safe cached stable target is available; it does not claim the panel is up to date.

current_version.description: The installed ha-paneld version observed with the cached update.

tag.description: Exact source release tag for target_version; not a URL.

HaPathProbe.description: Layer-3 ICMP echo measurement of the path to the address the Home Assistant socket is connected on. Intermittent, with an interval that widens while the path proves reliable. Reported only in this release; it does not raise the panel warning.

family.description: The address family the Home Assistant socket actually connected on; null when no route is held. Reported in every state, including unsupported.

other_resolved.description: Whether DNS also returned an address in the other family for this connected socket; null when no matching DNS result is known. Resolution is not reachability, and this field does not trigger a warning or another probe.

available.description: unsupported means the platform refuses the app an ICMP socket; unproven means no echo has been answered yet, so silence is not counted as loss.

interval_ms.description: The current burst interval, which adapts to how reliable the path has been.

HaNetworkPath.description: Rolling classification of the network path between the panel and its configured Home Assistant, measured as the round trip of Home Assistant WebSocket ping frames on the app's own authenticated socket over a five-minute window. Emitted unconditionally: Measurement is owned by an AUTHENTICATED socket, not by the demand for one: measuring is false and state is idle until the stream has reached an authenticated, subscribed connection, and again once it stops (no lifecycle, entity or registry demand for one, no credentials, or a stream parked on a refused sign-in or repeated protocol failures). While a socket that HAS been live is being re-established, measurement continues and socket reports reconnecting, because a broken path must still be reported during the outage it explains. warning means the rolling p95 exceeds 100 ms; severe means the p95 exceeds 1,000 ms, two consecutive probes went unanswered, or more than 5% of the window's probes went unanswered. One isolated miss or spike never alarms. Failures Home Assistant itself caused (closed or refused connection, protocol error, restart, sign-in refused, or a ping left unanswered while other frames still arrive) are counted as server_failures or auth_failures and never as network loss. Aggregates only; never a host, address or sample. Millisecond fields are -1 when no round trip is in the window.

state.description: The network PATH verdict: warning when probes are being lost, severe after a run of consecutive losses. Latency never raises it. settling is the startup period; idle means no authenticated socket is held.

responsiveness.description: How quickly Home Assistant answers on an intact path. A performance figure only; it never raises the network warning.

settling.description: True during the first three minutes after app start, when no verdict is formed.

probes.description: Round trips plus network failures in the window

jitter_ms.description: Mean absolute difference between successive round trips

last_round_trip_age_ms.description: How long ago the last probe was answered; -1 when none has been. An empty window with an age is a stream that stopped probing, not a fresh connect

socket.description: Whether the authenticated socket is up now or is being re-established; present only while measuring

RendererHealth.description: Sanitized state of the panel's dashboard renderer and its Home Assistant admission. Always present, including when an external renderer or no renderer is configured, so a consumer never infers applicability from an absent object. No URL, host, credential or raw exception text is exposed: the transport failure arrives already classified and fault_detail is a sanitized exception class name.

mode.description: Which renderer is configured. ha-paneld observes admission only for its own built-in renderer; a foreign renderer's Home Assistant connection is not visible to it.

state.description: rendered means admitted AND the Home Assistant frontend is connected now. admitted without rendered is a panel that started but shows no dashboard. unobserved is never a statement of health — it is a fresh process, a replaced renderer, or a renderer that is not running.

outcome.description: The last admission verdict. ok_cached means the live version check could not complete and a previously verified version admitted the renderer, so nothing about the server was confirmed this time.

fault.description: Transport failure classified from the exception type. none means no transport failure was involved; unknown means one occurred and was not classified — deliberately distinct.

fault_detail.description: Sanitized exception class name (letters, digits and underscore only, at most 40 characters) or http_<code>.

recovery.description: How a blocked verdict may recover unattended. manual_only will not clear without a person or a server change the panel cannot notice.

transport.description: Scheme of the configured Home Assistant endpoint. The scheme alone; never the URL or host.

address_family_policy.description: Configured address-family policy Home Assistant connections follow (automatic, prefer_ipv4, force_ipv4). A policy, not an observed connection: no client reports which address it reached.

observed_age_ms.description: How long ago the ADMISSION verdict was observed; null when nothing has been observed for the live renderer. Admission does not re-run once it passes, so on a healthy panel this is the age of the renderer generation rather than a measure of how recently the dashboard was seen working; state answers that.

process_age_ms.description: How long ago the process holding this observation started. The record is process-local and never persisted, so observed_age_ms can never legitimately exceed this.

package_updated_age_ms.description: How long ago this app package was last installed or replaced; null when the package manager would not say. A replacement kills the process, so evidence gathered after an upgrade is necessarily younger than this. Wall-clock, unlike the other ages here, because that is the only clock the package manager records against — allow a margin when comparing.

theme_policy.description: The configured dashboard_theme as a wire token.

theme_ambient.description: Under theme_policy ambient only: the scheme the room's light resolves the policy to now. Null while Ambient follows Home Assistant, and for every other policy.

theme_ambient_reason.description: Under theme_policy ambient only: why it resolves as it does. holding_source_unavailable keeps the last verdict while the light source is silent; waiting_for_verdict, auto_brightness_off and no_light_source follow Home Assistant. Null for every other policy.

theme_ambient_level.description: Under theme_policy ambient only: the room's last normalised light level from the auto-brightness model, 0 (its dark end) to 1 (its bright end), rounded to two places. Ambient turns dark at or below 0.40 and light at or above 0.55, each after the level has held there for 60 seconds.

theme_effective.description: The colour scheme the Home Assistant frontend reports it is rendering now, observed by the built-in renderer on connect and on every theme change. Null when there is no connected built-in page to observe.

theme_overridden.description: True when dashboard_theme forces a scheme and the connected frontend is rendering the other one. That is the documented precedence: an explicit Light or Dark chosen in Home Assistant wins over the panel's policy, because overriding it would mean writing the user's account-wide preference. This field exists so that case is never silent; summary and action then say so.

action.description: Actionable guidance for the current renderer state; empty when no action is required.

StorageHealth.description: Sanitized latest observation of the filesystem containing ha-paneld's SQLite database. No filesystem paths, configuration values or raw exception text are exposed. Metrics remain JSON null when their underlying probe is unavailable.

state.description: Overall state. database_failure takes precedence over the underlying pressure band.

pressure_state.description: Underlying filesystem/WAL pressure band, retained when state is database_failure.

database_bytes.description: Main database file size; excludes WAL and sidecars.

sidecar_bytes.description: Combined size of allowlisted SQLite sidecars other than the WAL.

freelist_count.description: Pages the database holds but is not using. A large value is not itself a fault — read it together with auto_vacuum, which says whether those pages can be returned to the filesystem at all.

auto_vacuum.description: SQLite's auto-vacuum mode for this database, which decides whether bounded freelist reclamation can run. Only incremental reclaims in slices. none is not a fault and is never converted implicitly, because enabling auto-vacuum needs a full VACUUM whose temporary-space demand can worsen a low-space incident. Until then its freelist pages cannot return to the filesystem; the only conversion is inside a full VACUUM that storage remediation admits under warning pressure (see remediation_vacuum).

checked_at.description: Unix epoch milliseconds for the underlying storage/SQLite check.

failure.description: Optional controlled failure kind; never raw exception text.

failure_operation.description: Optional controlled name of the operation that failed, drawn from a fixed internal vocabulary — for example catalog-maintenance, app-state-write or database-checkpoint. Anything outside that vocabulary is reported as the generic database, so no SQL, filesystem path, entity id or other user data can appear here. Present only alongside failure, and the field most likely to make an unknown failure reproducible.

remediation.description: Present only after this process has run automatic storage remediation. Judged from a fresh observation taken after the run: relieved means pressure cleared; deferred means a step met contention and a later run retries; exhausted means every safe step ran or was refused for a stated reason and pressure remains, so the operator must act; unverified means no completed observation followed the run. Remediation deletes only orphaned app-owned temporary files and expired history rows, never configuration or the database.

remediation_at.description: Unix epoch milliseconds when the last remediation run finished. Present with remediation.

remediation_freed_bytes.description: Bytes the last run measurably returned: deleted file sizes plus the measured shrink of the database and WAL files. Present with remediation.

remediation_retention.description: Expired-history pruning in the last run. Refused at critical pressure, because deleting rows costs WAL space before any is returned. Present with remediation.

remediation_wal_checkpoint.description: Truncating WAL checkpoint in the last run, admitted on a fresh observation taken after history pruning and an ownership check immediately before it. deferred_busy is contention, not a fault; skipped_lifecycle means shutdown or a data backup or restore began first; skipped_unobserved means no completed observation followed pruning; failed is also latched as a database failure. Present with remediation.

remediation_vacuum.description: Full VACUUM in the last run. It is admitted only below critical pressure, with measured headroom, a worthwhile freelist that bounded reclamation cannot reach, a verified configuration backup and lifecycle ownership. Present with remediation.

remediation_vacuum_refusal.description: Why the full VACUUM was refused. Present only when remediation_vacuum is refused.

PowerSafety.description: Conservative app-owned assessment of panel reachability after screen-off. A guard needed to establish safety is never inferred from an unavailable probe, and no individual setting is treated as proof against OEM suspend behaviour.

repair_capability.description: Exact capability for Android global/Doze mutation; helper and generic shell routes do not count.

acknowledge_available.description: True only for a caution with healthy app-owned guards and no supported system-power mutator.

acknowledged.description: Presentation suppression only; state, warning and diagnostics remain unchanged.

acknowledgement_fingerprint.description: Opaque exact-state token accepted only while the same caution and capability remain current.

power_source.description: Android-reported source only; android_reports_unplugged does not claim the panel is physically unplugged.

screen_off_mechanism.description: The declared screen-off route (the profile's `hardware.screen_off` intent), regardless of what the runtime actually used.

screen_off_selected.description: The route the runtime actually used on the last screen-off, which can differ from screen_off_mechanism (a fallback transport, or a degrade to brightness-only). Null before any screen-off has occurred since this controller was constructed.

screen_off_reason.description: Explains screen_off_selected: matches the declared route, fell back to the other transport, degraded to brightness-only, or not yet exercised.

CameraHealth.description: Sanitized state of the panel's on-device camera session (off by default; see the camera privacy rules). Always present, including on a board with no camera at all, so a consumer never infers applicability from an absent object. No frame, client address, credential or raw exception text is exposed: the fault arrives already classified and fault_detail is a sanitized exception class name. The stream_* and encode_* fields describe the one RTSP H.264 encode session (video only; rtsp://<panel>:<stream_port>/live, with ?res=, ?fps= and ?kbps= overriding the configured camera_resolution / camera_fps / camera_kbps defaults in either direction); delivered_fps and delivered_kbps are what the encoder actually produced over the last few seconds, and summary names the stream URL while the transport is listening.

state.description: absent means this board offers no camera, with fault_detail naming which of the three reasons it is. idle means enabled, permitted and closed because nobody is watching — idle cost is zero. degraded means the bounded retry ceiling was reached; the session stays visibly here until a subscriber reattaches or the user acts.

outcome.description: Wire form of the last outcome: ok, or the refusal token that last blocked a consumer. A refusal is cleared when a session opens for a client; camera-disabled is additionally cleared the moment the camera setting turns on again, so an idle, enabled camera reads ok rather than refused. Every other refusal stands until a session opens, and camera-disabled itself is replaced rather than cleared when the camera is still refusing for its own reasons at that moment, such as an encoder hold, a retry backoff or a camera that has given up; state and fault then say which. The token is one of camera-unavailable, camera-disabled, camera-permission-needed, camera-indication-unavailable, camera-foreground-refused, camera-starved, camera-encode-failed, camera-stream-encoder-unavailable or camera-stopping. camera-unavailable is shared by an absent camera and by a device open/configure failure; state and fault disambiguate which one occurred. camera-encode-failed means a frame arrived but would not encode as JPEG. camera-stream-encoder-unavailable means a stream was refused because no hardware H.264 encoder fits the caps or the running one failed; snapshots are unaffected. The RTSP transport additionally answers camera-busy (in its X-Camera header) when it already serves its maximum number of clients.

fault.description: Closed vocabulary the fault is classified into. A raw exception message never becomes one of these; only its sanitized class name enters fault_detail. none means nothing is faulted; encode means the last JPEG could not be produced although the camera delivered; stream_encoder means the hardware H.264 encoder could not be opened within the caps or failed while streaming.

fault_detail.description: Sanitized exception class name (or similarly bounded classification text); null when fault is none and the state is not absent. While state is absent it carries the capability reason instead: suppressed_by_profile (the profile sets hardware.camera false), not_enumerated (the profile is silent and Android enumerated no camera) or undetermined (the enumeration has not answered yet, which is not a statement about the hardware). A profile that declares a camera the board does not expose is not absent at all: the capability holds and every open fails with no_camera_id.

recovery.description: How a degraded state may recover on its own, or none when nothing is degraded.

clients.description: Subscribers currently holding the camera session open.

last_frame_age_ms.description: Age of the last real CAPTURED frame in milliseconds, never the age of a verdict or a state change; null when no frame has ever been captured. Named deliberately unlike the renderer's observed_age_ms, which measures an admission verdict rather than a sighting — that distinction was misread once.

consecutive_failures.description: Consecutive session failures counted toward the bounded retry ceiling.

indication.description: Which route is currently telling the room the camera is on. none is only legal when the camera is closed.

stream_clients.description: RTSP clients among clients, each holding the session open through its own lease.

stream_port.description: The RTSP port (8554) while the stream transport is listening, which it does exactly while camera_enabled is on and a camera is declared by the profile or enumerated by Android; null when it is off or the port could not be bound.

requested_fps.description: Frame rate the current stream asked for, which encode_fps does not always equal: the capture rate is fixed by whoever opens the session, so a stream that joins a session a snapshot already opened is encoded at the configured default however much it asked for. Null while no stream lease is held, and the first current lease's request when two streams share the session.

encoder.description: The MediaCodec hardware H.264 encoder currently running, or null while no stream client holds the session.

encode_width.description: Width the running encoder is bound to; null while no encoder runs. The encode is bound once, by the first stream client's URL parameters within the caps; later clients join it.

encode_fps.description: Frame-rate the encoder is fed at, a ceiling enforced where frames enter it.

encode_kbps.description: Bitrate target the running encoder was configured with. A stream URL may override the configured camera_kbps default upward or downward within the product range.

delivered_fps.description: Frames per second the encoder actually emitted over the last few seconds, to one decimal; null until it has emitted two.

delivered_kbps.description: Kilobits per second the encoder actually emitted over the same window — the measurement of whether the bitrate target is honoured.

snapshot_exposure.description: How the last answered snapshot got its frame. A snapshot waits for the sensor to report converged auto-exposure, because the first frames off a cold sensor are badly under-exposed, but only for a bounded budget so that a device which never reports CONTROL_AE_STATE still returns a picture. converged means the sensor settled; budget means the wait was spent and the frame was handed over unsettled, which is the one case that may still be dark; none means no snapshot has been answered yet.

snapshot_exposure_fallbacks.description: How many snapshots the settle budget has answered without convergence since the panel's camera owner was created. Zero alongside snapshot_exposure converged is a sensor reporting its exposure state normally.

action.description: Actionable guidance for the current camera state; none when no action is required. Every absent state carries one, because a panel offering no camera is the case most in need of saying what would change the answer.

ApprovalRequired.description: This high-impact remote request requires someone physically at the panel to approve it on the panel's screen; it cannot be approved remotely. Retry the identical request from the same peer within 10 minutes. Approval is one-use and process-local.

get.summary: Versioned liveness probe
get.description: The response also carries pa_notice=1 while an unconnected panel owes its owner the migration notice, or pa_notice=0 when connected or dismissed for this versionCode. This token is always present on both /health and /api/v1/health.

200.description: Version, panel id, build token and config hash. An optional `did=<64 lower-case hexadecimal characters>` token is the domain-separated pseudonymous Panel Assistant discovery identity; it is derived from the persistent per-install identity and omitted when that identity is unavailable. The `identity=install` token explicitly marks per-install identity semantics whenever `did` is present. An optional `legacy_did=<64 lower-case hexadecimal characters>` token carries the previous Android-ID digest solely as an upgrade hint; it is never a session identity. A `pkg=<application id>` token names the installed package that answered, and a `vc=<integer>` token carries its Android version code, the build number that tells two builds of one version apart. While the panel is watching Home Assistant lifecycle events a trailing `ha=<state>` token is appended, one of `normal`, `shutting_down`, `starting`, `back_online` or `connection_lost`; the token is absent entirely when the panel is not watching. A third token `ha_refused=1` is appended when the panel is watching but Home Assistant refused the lifecycle subscription, so a reader can tell a refused watch from an absent one. Every one of these tokens is appended only when it applies, so the line is unchanged for a reader that does not know them; a reader that counts fields rather than parsing tokens will see more. A second token `ha_src=<socket|mqtt|native>` names which source observed the state and is present only when one did: `socket` is Home Assistant's own lifecycle event and proves intent, `native` is Panel Assistant’s installation-wide lifecycle notice, whereas `mqtt` is the broker publishing Home Assistant's will, which also fires if Home Assistant merely loses its broker link and therefore states only that the control path is gone. States the panel infers locally — the initial `normal`, and a `connection_lost` noticed from its own transport — carry no `ha_src`. While watching, `ha_reason=<restart|host_reboot|core_update|unknown>` names the reported reason; unknown makes no claim about intent. Optional `ha_elapsed_ms` and `ha_expected_ms` report elapsed and historically measured expected duration. `ha_grace_ms` reports remaining slack before an unexplained loss is displayed (initially 10000 ms); deliberate notices display immediately. While the panel holds an authenticated Home Assistant socket for any reason (the built-in renderer watching lifecycle events, an ambient light or presence entity source, or a registry watch) five further tokens report the measured network path to Home Assistant from the app's own WebSocket probes: `ha_net=<healthy|warning|severe>` is the rolling five-minute verdict, `ha_net_p95=<ms>` the nearest-rank p95 round trip (-1 when no probe has answered), `ha_net_n=<count>` the probes in the window, `ha_net_miss=<count>` the probes that went unanswered and `ha_net_age=<ms>` how long ago the last probe was answered (-1 when none has been), which separates a socket that has only just connected from a stream that stopped probing. A probe that goes unanswered while any other frame keeps arriving, including a late pong for an abandoned earlier probe, is counted as a server failure, never as loss, and the socket stays up. `ha_resp=<healthy|warning|severe>` classifies how quickly Home Assistant answers on a path that is intact; it is a performance figure and never raises the network warning, which is reserved for evidence that packets are being lost. `ha_net=settling` is reported alone for the first three minutes after the app starts, while startup load makes the round trip describe the panel rather than the path. All of them are absent when the path is not measured (the panel holds no Home Assistant socket); a healthy verdict is reported explicitly rather than by omission. No host, address or individual sample is ever included.

parameters.name: X-Panel-Assistant-Update-Owner
parameters.description: Sent by a Panel Assistant config entry while its own ha-paneld update entity is registered and enabled. Exactly 1 renews a 24-hour lease during which the panel withholds its MQTT ha-paneld update entity, so Home Assistant never shows two. Any other value is ignored. It grants no authority.

200.description: Health warnings plus structured component snapshots. renderer, camera, storage_health, ha_network and power_safety are always present; panel_assistant_update is additive and never starts a release lookup, unavailable or incomplete fresh probes produce unknown rather than safe, a renderer with nothing observed reports unobserved rather than health, and a board with no camera reports the camera object's absent state rather than omitting it.

install_capability.description: Live self-update installer route available inside the app: api means su, the compatible root helper, or locally approved Shizuku can run the signer-pinned app installer; none means no such route. This is not a guarantee that a particular APK passes its own admission. Home Assistant may separately prove an ADB route.

database_observation_nonce.description: Same-request freshness proof; present only when requested with a valid nonce and the database observation completed cleanly

panel_assistant_update.description: Additive cached stable ha-paneld update observation. It carries no URL, channel, release prose or operation state; read /api/v1/install/status for a running panel-owned transaction.

home_ui.description: Present only for home_proof=1. ready proves a foreground dashboard and resolved HOME; setup proves an app administration activity is visible; blocked and unknown never complete an update.

panel_assistant_device.description: Additive device-identity projection for the Panel Assistant integration's device card. Panels below the release that introduced it omit the property entirely.
